newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FOCUS-Malaysia Perwaja Steel "to make profit by '98".
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Malaysia Perwaja Steel "to make profit by '98".

text.p: Rescuers of Malaysia's Perwaja Steel Sdn Bhd need to invest more than a billion ringgit ($400 million) to revive the ailing national steel company, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Thursday.
"If we have the confidence, I feel we can revive this plant," Mahathir was quoted as saying by the national Bernama news agency after a visit to the plant in eastern Terengganu state.

Equal Concept Sdn Bhd, which will run Perwaja until the government finds it a partner, said on Thursday it was confident the steel plant could make a net profit of 100 million ringgit ($39.7 million) by 1998.
By 2000, Perwaja's profit was expected to double to 200 million ringgit, Bernama quoted Equal's chief executive Abu Talib Mohamed as saying.
Company and government officials were not immediately available to confirm the Bernama reports.
Mahathir said the rescuers of Perwaja need to invest more than a billion ringgit to revive the steel company.

Perwaja, a 10-year-old pet project of Mahathir, was found earlier this year to have accumulated losses of 2.9 billion ringgit and its previous government-appointed managers were accused of financial mismanagement.
Abu Talib said since taking over Perwaja in July, Equal Concept has cut the steel plant's costs by 40 percent or 200 ringgit through the production of "high value" materials.
Efforts were being made to cut another 200 ringgit in output costs by boosting production and maintaining factory equipment properly, he said.
Abu Talib said Perwaja would be rolling out a new stainless steel grade by early 1998 and saw a strong demand for steel products until 2000.

He said a forged steel grade introduced by Perwaja two months ago for making automotive components had an encouraging response. Sales for this was estimated at between 20,000-25,000 tonnes annually, he said.
Abu Talib said the equity structure in Perwaja would be left to the government, which was considering various options such as state-guaranteed loans to rebuild the company's finances.

Equal Concept, a joint-venture between Maju Holdings Sdn Bhd and the Lion Group, was formed to rescue Perwaja. But Lion backed out after it expressed displeasure with the 30 percent stake offered to it, as compared to Maju's 51 percent.

Mahathir said it was imperative that Perwaja be successful as the project reflected the capability of the country's indigenous Malays, or Bumiputra, and his government wanted to recoup the money invested.
"Perwaja was my idea, if it fails, I will be embarrassed," he said.
